verdict_reason: One verified production defect (double-scheme notification CTA URL — dead email link to landlords on every reference event); remainder are a coverage gate (AC7 abuse 0%) and lower-severity hygiene/contract gaps.

findings.title: Reference notifications pass a scheme-full origin to build_entity_url → double-scheme 'https://https://…' dead CTA in every reference email
findings.evidence: form_handler.gleam:1309 `let origin = domain_helpers.origin_from_domain(row.origin_domain)` — origin_from_domain returns scheme-full `"https://" <> domain`; passed as origin_domain to notify_reference_completed/declined/objected → dispatch_reference_notification → email_client.build_entity_url which does `"https://" <> domain <> path`. Precedent notify_application_scored (ai_client.gleam:1927) passes the RAW `vacancy_row.origin_domain` (scheme-less) → correct URL.
findings.detail: build_entity_url always prepends https://. The new handlers feed it an already-schemed origin, so every reference notification email's 'View application' CTA is 'https://https://righttenantry.ie/vacancies/<id>/applications/<id>' — a dead link landlords cannot click.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass the raw row.origin_domain to the three notify_reference_* calls (matching the notify_application_scored precedent), not origin_from_domain(row.origin_domain). Reserve origin_from_domain for the invite base_url where a scheme is needed.

findings.title: focus_seconds_reported is always 0 in production — the review submit form omits the _focus_seconds field; the integration test masks the gap by injecting it
findings.evidence: view_review's submit form renders honeypot + timing + button only; _focus_seconds is rendered only by form_question_pages.gleam:84 (the per-question form). reference_form.js:157 fills [data-focus-seconds] only if present. parse_focus_seconds returns 0 for absent. The test injects #("_focus_seconds","240").
findings.detail: The submit POST originates from the review page, which never carries _focus_seconds, so fraud_signals.form_session.focus_seconds_reported is structurally always 0 in production — contradicting the dev record ('rc3-4 captures focus_seconds_reported') and starving rc3-7's focus-time signal.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a _focus_seconds hidden input (data-focus-seconds) to the review submit form in view_review so reference_form.js populates it; stop injecting it in the test.

findings.title: decline_reason has no server-side bound — crafted POST stores unbounded free text into the result JSONB (/apply truncates identical fields to 2000 graphemes)
findings.evidence: apply_decline reads decline_reason verbatim into minimal_terminal_result(note: Some(text)) → json.string(text), no truncate. form_pages.gleam:447 maxlength="200" (client only). application_handler.gleam:1772/1788/1802 truncate eviction_details/reason_for_moving/pet_details via truncate(2000).
findings.detail: The only length cap on the optional reason is the client-side maxlength; a crafted POST bypasses it. The value rides reference_call.result JSONB (the compliance-relevant store RC4 + DSAR exports will render). The /apply precedent truncates; decline does not.
findings.recommended_fix: Pipe decline_reason through application_handler.truncate(200) (or 2000 to match /apply) before persisting, server-side.

findings.title: AC7 abuse posture has ZERO coverage on the four new exit-route POSTs — incl. the load-bearing stop-must-not-object branch
findings.evidence: Every exit-route integration test sends timing_fields() = [#("_website",""),#("_form_loaded_at",…)] — a clean honeypot. No test fills the honeypot or trips timing on submit/decline/stop/wrong-person. handle_stop_post's fake-success-without-objecting branch (the 'critical' AC7 case) is unpinned.
findings.detail: A regression objecting on a fake stop (silently opting out real referees if a token leaked) would pass CI. The guard is correct in the code; the coverage is absent. AC7 = NONE.
findings.recommended_fix: Add integration tests: honeypot-filled POST to /stop → 200 stop-confirmed, row stays contact_initiated, objection_log count 0; same for decline/wrong-person/submit.

findings.title: notify_reference_completed/declined/objected + the late_after_handoff branch have no test pins
findings.evidence: grep of server/test for notify_reference_* / ReferenceCompleted / ReferenceDeclined / ReferenceObjected: 0 matches. AC1/AC3/AC4 'dispatches' clauses unpinned.
findings.detail: No assertion of the in-app notification row, the maybe_send_email preference gate, or the taken_over_at late-completion copy. Because notify_reference_event discards the dispatch Result, a broken dispatch passes CI silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an integration test asserting the notification row is created per event + the late-completion copy fires when taken_over_at is set.

findings.title: The four new audit terminal events are written but never asserted — the audit-on-status-change invariant is unpinned for these transitions
findings.evidence: grep of the new suite for reference_call_completed/declined/objected/wrong_person + audit_log: 0 matches.
findings.detail: AGENTS.md's defended invariant 'Audit-log writes fire on … status changes' stays unpinned for the form_completed/refused/objected/awaiting_correction transitions rc3-4 introduces.
findings.recommended_fix: Query audit_log in the per-path integration tests for the expected event_type + entity_id.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: FAIL (AC7 P0 = 0%, overall ≈72% < 80%)
findings.evidence: Per-AC coverage: AC1 55%, AC2 80%, AC3 57%, AC4 63%, AC5 100%, AC6 90%, AC7 0%, AC8 100%, AC9 100% → overall ≈72%. AC5 (objection stickiness) and AC8 (registry coverage) tests are genuinely biting. Unit suite green (server 1418, integration 448).
findings.detail: Gate fails primarily on AC7 (abuse coverage) and several unpinned-but-correct AC1/AC3/AC4 dispatch/stamp clauses. No active defect beyond the CTA URL; the fail is a coverage signal.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin AC7 (W3), the notification dispatch (W4), and the audit writes (W5) to lift P0/P1 above threshold.

findings.title: character_ref verification block omits the spec-pinned free_text_signals[] field
findings.evidence: character_verification emits identity/relationship/capacity/known_duration/character_statement/would_stand_again — no free_text_signals. Spec line 163 lists free_text_signals[] for character_ref; landlord (139) + employer (158) emit it.
findings.detail: Data-equivalent today (the character form has no free-text question), but the pinned AD-9 shape is incomplete for downstream RC4 readers.
findings.recommended_fix: Emit free_text_signals as json.array([], json.string) (or from a future character free-text question) for shape parity.

findings.title: headline() LandlordRef has two identical arms — the `_, ""` arm is shadowed by `_, _`
findings.evidence: `_, "" -> "Tenancy: " <> unknownish(tenancy) <> "."` followed by `_, _ -> "Tenancy: " <> unknownish(tenancy) <> "."` — identical strings.
findings.detail: The second-to-last arm is unreachable (the final arm covers it); the intended distinct 'pay present but unknown' rendering isn't expressed.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the redundant `_, ""` arm or give it a distinct message.

findings.title: An objector re-visiting the token is told 'This reference was declined.' — classify collapses Refused|Objected → Declined
findings.evidence: classify maps Refused | Objected -> Declined; view_declined renders title 'This reference was declined.' An objector asked to STOP contact, not decline.
findings.detail: Factually wrong copy for the objector in an honest-first design. The collapse is the rc3-3 classify design; the copy is the mismatch.
findings.recommended_fix: Either a distinct view_objected state page, or copy that reads truthfully for both refused + objected.

findings.title: form_session.completion_seconds is null at submit — spec Dev Notes pin it as rc3-4's job, Completion Notes defer to rc3-7
findings.evidence: form_session_fraud_signals emits completion_seconds: json.null(). Spec result-structuring Dev Notes say rc3-4 stamps completion_seconds from form_opened_at→submitted_at; the minion's Completion Notes defer it to rc3-7. Implementation follows the Completion Notes.
findings.detail: Internal spec contradiction. The implementation is deterministic and honest (null), and the row's form_opened_at + submitted_at are stamped so rc3-7 can compute it — but the pinned AD-9 form_session shape is partially empty at submit.
findings.recommended_fix: Resolve the spec contradiction; if rc3-4 owns it, compute completion_seconds from the stamped timestamps now.

findings.title: AC8 CSRF-stack test asserts only not_equal(403), weaker than the spec-pinned 2xx/3xx reachability assertion
findings.evidence: csrf_stack_skips_every_new_exit_route_post_test asserts `should.not_equal(403)`. Spec Dev Notes pin 'asserting 2xx/3xx (not a 403 CSRF rejection)'.
findings.detail: A 404 (missing arm) or 500 would pass not_equal(403); the pin proves no-403, not reachability.
findings.recommended_fix: Tighten to assert the status is in {200,303} (or the expected per-route status).

findings.title: Claimed 'telegram' ✗ negative-control bite-test for the widened channel CHECK does not exist
findings.evidence: grep of server/test + supabase for 'telegram': 0 matches. The 'web' ✓ half exists (stop_post_objects_and_writes_evidence_once_test asserts channel='web'); the 'telegram' ✗ half the dev record claims is absent.
findings.detail: The widened CHECK constraint is correct (migration is sound), but the negative control proving it still bites is missing — overclaim in the dev record.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test asserting an INSERT with channel='telegram' violates the CHECK (or document that the integration suite's 'web' insert is the sole pin).

findings.title: parse_focus_seconds accepts negative / unbounded client values, stored verbatim into fraud_signals
findings.evidence: parse_focus_seconds uses int.parse(text) with no floor/ceiling; int.parse accepts a leading minus, so _focus_seconds=-7 is stored as focus_seconds_reported.
findings.detail: Client-reported fraud input stored with no bounds. Moot in production today (the field is absent from the review form — see W1 — so it's 0), but reachable via a crafted POST and would poison rc3-7's signal.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp to max(0, parsed) (and an upper bound) before storing.

findings.title: purge_after is stamped only by the submit terminal; refused/objected keep it NULL despite the column contract 'stamped at terminal'
findings.evidence: complete_reference_call.sql stamps purge_after (CASE … $4::timestamptz); terminalize_reference_call.sql does not touch purge_after. Migration comment: 'purge_after TIMESTAMPTZ, -- stamped at terminal'. Partial index idx_reference_call_purge WHERE purge_after IS NOT NULL excludes refused/objected.
findings.detail: No purge sweep exists yet (rc3-5+), so impact is deferred; referee PII in those rows still rides application CASCADE + the retention job. But when a sweep ships it will structurally miss refused/objected rows unless it handles them.
findings.recommended_fix: Stamp purge_after in terminalize_reference_call too (decline/objection follow the same retention schedule), or document the exclusion.

findings.title: Exit handlers omit handle_resend's injectable seam; notify_reference_event discards the dispatch Result
findings.evidence: handle_resend uses resend_with_send(config, old_token, row, send_fn) with an injectable ResendSend seam; the new exit handlers bind directly. notify_reference_event does `let _ = case event {…}` discarding the Result.
findings.detail: The spec's pattern-fidelity block names the injectable seam; the exits drop it. Discarded dispatch Result + no notify tests (W4) means a broken dispatch is invisible to CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Either restore an injectable seam for the terminal flows, or at minimum assert the dispatch path in tests (W4) so the discarded Result is still observed.

findings.title: ObjectionChannel shared enum lacks the 'web' variant the new migration adds to the DB CHECK (documented drift)
findings.evidence: The migration widens channel CHECK to include 'web'; the shared ObjectionChannel enum does not. The single writer passes the raw string 'web', so inert today.
findings.detail: Documented by the minion ('noted for a future story'). The future inbound-email second writer + the existing encode_objection_channel codecs cannot represent 'web' until the enum is widened.
findings.recommended_fix: Add Web to ObjectionChannel in the same story that adds the second writer (inbound-email objection), or now if cheap.

findings.title: Objection evidence INSERT is not atomic with the guarded terminal UPDATE — a crash between leaves an objected row with no Art 21 evidence (documented best-effort)
findings.evidence: apply_objection: sql.terminalize_reference_call (UPDATE, autocommit) THEN insert_objection_evidence (INSERT) as two pog.execute calls, no transaction. A crash/connection drop in the window → status='objected' with no reference_objection_log row; the INSERT is never retried (every later tap hits the 0-row branch).
findings.detail: Documented as best-effort in the handler doc. The referee's request is still honoured (status flipped → sends stop); the loss is the Art 21 evidence trail. A transaction (or a retry) would close the window.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap the guarded UPDATE + evidence INSERT in a single pog transaction, or add a reconciliation/retry for the evidence row.

findings.title: purge_after / submitted_at / denormalised fraud_signals column are never asserted at submit
findings.evidence: grep of new tests for purge_after/submitted_at/fraud_signals: 0 matches. AC1 pins schema_version/channel/outcome/verification-present/next_attempt_at only.
findings.detail: A bug in the $4='' purge_after CASE, the submitted_at stamp, or the fraud_signals denormalised write would go unnoticed.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert submitted_at IS NOT NULL, fraud_signals IS NOT NULL, and purge_after tracks retention_due_at in the submit test.

findings.title: AC2 one-submission pin asserts only the 303, not that nothing re-persisted
findings.evidence: second_submit_redirects_to_the_state_page_test asserts second.status == 303; no assertion that result/submitted_at/audit are unchanged.
findings.detail: Low risk: the handler redirects via classify before any write, so no duplicate path is reachable — but the pin doesn't prove the no-re-persist contract directly.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture submitted_at/audit count before the second POST; assert unchanged after.

findings.title: The three GET confirm pages are untested, incl. AC4's pre-fetch-safe stop GET (mutates nothing)
findings.evidence: The integration suite POSTs every exit route; no GET of /decline, /stop, /wrong-person. form_pages_test covers rc3-3 pages only.
findings.detail: AC4's 'GET mutates nothing' (prefetch safety — a GET that objected would silently opt out referees) is unpinned. Low risk given exit_get renders the page without writes, but the safety property deserves a pin.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a GET /stop test asserting status 200 + status unchanged + objection_log count 0.
